verdict.summary: Creating and testing your own Clio Manage app is quick and needs no approval. Listing the app for other firms in the App Directory adds a security review, a demo, and a listing review, and Clio has not published a timeline for those steps.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1 (own account): about 1-2 hours of active work (estimate, not sourced). Directory listing: several days of work plus an unpublished review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes to hours once you have a paid Clio login or a developer account (estimate; app creation is a short form).
verdict.approval_wait: Not published. Clio aims to answer the security questionnaire request within 2 business days; demo and listing timing are not documented.

gates.name: Own account (no approval)
gates.unlocks: Create a Developer Application, connect your own Clio Manage account, and run the full OAuth flow and API calls against it.
limits: Clio offers no sandbox; test on your own developer account, not customer accounts.
Default API rate limit is 50 requests per minute during peak hours, per access token; custom increases are not supported for applications.
Access tokens last 30 days; refresh tokens do not expire.
One Developer Application is needed per region you serve.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes once you have a paid Clio login or an approved free developer account. Developer account approval timing is not published.

gates.name: Private app for a single firm (not listed)
gates.unlocks: Clio distinguishes private apps built for one client or law firm from public apps. A private app is not listed in the App Directory.
limits: Clio's docs do not state any user cap or install cap for unlisted or private apps.
The same 50 requests per minute peak rate limit applies.
Whether an unlisted public app can be installed by other firms without review is not documented.
gates.time_to_reach: Same as Gate 1 once the firm's account and app are set up.

gates.name: App Directory listing (public)
gates.unlocks: Publication in the Clio App Directory and placement inside Clio Manage (App Integrations) for any firm.
limits: Security review and a 30-minute demo with API Partnerships are required before launch.
Must support the latest two versions of major browsers, which Clio may ask you to demonstrate.
Core functionality must show at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis.
App Integrations placement requires the app to be listed or approved for listing, and working Add to Clio support.
gates.time_to_reach: Not published. Security questionnaire target is 2 business days; demo, listing draft review and launch have no stated timeline.

steps.title: Confirm you are in the Clio Manage portal
steps.detail: Use the Clio Manage Developer Portal at developers.clio.com/apps, which sits behind a Clio login. Do not use the Clio Platform (Grow) portal at developers.api.clio.com, which is a separate product.
gotchas: A community guide describes the path as Settings → Developer Applications on the US app host. Use the developer portal above as the official entry point.

steps.title: Get a login with access to build
steps.detail: If you are building for your own practice or one firm, get login credentials for an existing paid Clio account from the firm's account admin. If you are building generally, request a free developer account through the Developer Hub form; a partnership team member will follow up by email. A seven-day trial account can also be converted by applying.
steps.est_time: 15 min to submit; wait time unknown
gotchas: Developer account approval criteria and timing are not published.

steps.title: Create the Developer Application
steps.detail: In the developer portal, create a new Developer Application. Enter the name, website URL, and at least one redirect URI. Add a description, icon, support URL and deauthorization callback URL only if you need them. Accept the Developer Terms of Service and select your access permissions.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URI must match exactly; Clio treats registered URIs as an allow-list.
Only the name, website URL, redirect URI, Terms acceptance and permissions are required.

steps.title: Choose the smallest permission set
steps.detail: Set each Clio Manage access permission to read-only or read/write. Request only what the app needs. Changing permissions later does not change existing grants, so users must re-authorize to receive the new permissions.
gotchas: Clio's docs do not say which permissions are sensitive or whether write access triggers extra review.

steps.title: Register one app per region
steps.detail: Clio integrations are local to each regional instance, and a token from one region is not valid in another. If you need US and Canadian customers, create a separate Developer Application in each region. Each region uses its own OAuth host.
gotchas: EU, CA and AU use their own hosts. Confirm the exact host for each region before you configure Composio.

steps.title: Copy the key and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID (key) and Client secret from the Developer Application. Enter them in your Composio auth config for Clio Manage. Composio has no managed Clio app, so this custom app is required.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Whether Composio accepts a custom Clio key and secret was not verified in this research. Test the connection before relying on it.

steps.title: Run a test authorization on your own account
steps.detail: Start the authorization code flow with your own paid or developer login. The authorization code expires after 10 minutes, so exchange it promptly. The token exchange is a form-encoded POST to the token URL with the key, secret, code and redirect_uri.

values.label: Token request
values.value: POST form-encoded: client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code

gotchas: Whether PKCE is supported on the Clio Manage authorize flow is not confirmed. The PKCE option seen was on the Clio Platform (Grow) form.

steps.title: Plan token storage and refresh
steps.detail: Store refresh tokens encrypted; they do not expire. Access tokens last 30 days (expires_in 2592000). Refresh with grant_type refresh_token plus client credentials, and replace the stored access token with the new one.
gotchas: The documented refresh response returns a new access token and no new refresh token. Whether refresh tokens rotate was not stated, so keep the old refresh token until you confirm.

steps.title: Design around the rate limit
steps.detail: Budget API calls to stay under 50 requests per minute per access token during peak hours. Handle 429 responses with backoff. Custom limit increases are not available for applications.

values.label: Default rate limit
values.value: 50 requests per minute at peak, per access token

steps.title: Set the deauthorization callback (optional)
steps.detail: If you need to know when a user revokes access, enter a deauthorization callback URL in the application form. Clio POSTs a JSON notice containing client_id, user_id and access_token to that URL when a token is revoked.

steps.title: Test only on your own data
steps.detail: Clio provides no sandbox for the Manage API. Test on your own developer or practice account and do not test against customer accounts.

steps.title: Decide whether you need directory listing
steps.detail: If the app only serves one firm, a private app is enough and is not listed in the directory. If other firms will install it, you need the App Directory listing and the review path below. Clio's docs do not state a user or install cap for unlisted apps.

steps.title: Request the security questionnaire
steps.detail: Email api.partnerships@clio.com to start the security review and ask for the questionnaire. Clio aims to respond within two business days. An older help-center article describes emailing a link and sample credentials instead, so confirm the current process when you write.
gotchas: The two sources differ on the submission method. Confirm with API Partnerships.

steps.title: Prepare the questionnaire, demo and listing draft
steps.detail: Draft answers for the security questionnaire, a demo script that covers the core flow, and the listing outline with integration onboarding content. Check that the app supports the latest two versions of major browsers and that core functionality can show 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis.

values.label: Browser support
values.value: Latest two versions of major browsers

steps.title: Book the demo and submit the listing
steps.detail: After security sign-off, book the 30-minute demo with the API Partnerships team and send them a pre-recorded demo. After the listing outline is complete, submit it for draft review. Clio's launch sequence is security questionnaire, demo, listing form and draft review, then launch.
steps.est_time: 1-2 hours of your time plus provider wait
gotchas: Clio does not publish a timeline for the demo, listing review or launch.

steps.title: Request App Integrations placement
steps.detail: Once the app is listed or approved for listing and Add to Clio works, email the App Integrations team with the app name and listing URL to request placement inside Clio Manage.

steps.title: Wait for Clio review
steps.detail: Clio reviews the security questionnaire, demo and listing draft. No review timeline is published beyond the two-business-day questionnaire target, so plan for an open-ended wait.

requirements.item: Developer account or paid Clio login
requirements.detail: You need login credentials on an existing paid Clio account from the firm admin, or an approved free developer account (trial conversion also possible).
Accepting Clio's Developer Terms of Service is required to create the application.
The redirect_uri in each authorize request must match a registered URI exactly.
Public app developers can start building without approval.
Each region needs its own Developer Application; tokens do not cross regions.
Passing a security review is required for App Directory listing.
A 30-minute demo is booked once security is signed off.
Latest two versions of major browsers, and 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis, are launch requirements.

scopes.scope: Clio Manage access permissions (read-only or read/write, per permission)
scopes.effect: Chosen per app in the developer portal. Request the smallest set. Changing them later needs user re-authorization. Clio has not documented which permissions are sensitive or restricted or whether write access adds review.

scopes.scope: offline_access, offline, openid, clio_user_info (Clio Identity SSO scopes)
scopes.effect: These come from Clio Identity's OpenID discovery document under account.clio.com. They are separate from the Clio Manage API permissions and were not covered in the Manage docs. Do not confuse them with Manage permissions.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect or OAuth error after login.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the request does not exactly match a URI registered in the Developer Application. Clio treats the list as an allow-list.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the application's redirect URI list, save, and retry. Confirm the scheme, host and path match character for character.

blockers.symptom: API calls return HTTP 429 during peak hours.
blockers.cause: The default limit is 50 requests per minute per access token at peak. Clio does not support custom increases for applications.
blockers.fix: Throttle and back off on 429. Reduce calls per token, and plan around the off-peak higher limits rather than expecting a raised cap.

blockers.symptom: A token from a US app does not work for Canadian (or EU/AU) customers.
blockers.cause: Clio integrations are local to each regional instance. Tokens do not cross regions.
blockers.fix: Create a separate Developer Application in each region and use that region's OAuth host for its customers.

blockers.symptom: No sandbox is available to test the integration.
blockers.cause: Clio provides no test or sandbox environment for the Manage API.
blockers.fix: Test on your own developer or practice account. Do not use customer accounts for testing.

blockers.symptom: App cannot be listed in the App Directory or placed in Clio Manage.
blockers.cause: Directory listing requires passing a security review, a demo and a listing review. Placement inside Clio Manage requires a listing or approval for listing.
blockers.fix: Email api.partnerships@clio.com to start the security questionnaire, then follow the demo and listing steps. Plan for an unpublished review wait.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Clio. Register your own Clio Manage Developer Application and supply its key and secret to Composio. Scopes are Clio access permissions chosen in the developer portal, not Composio defaults. Use the regional OAuth host for your customers' region. Whether Composio accepts a custom Clio key and secret was not verified.

evidence.claim: Creating a Developer Application in the Developer Portal is the first build step for Clio Manage.
evidence.quote: The first step when building an integration is to create a new Developer Application in the Developer Portal.

evidence.claim: The application form requires a name, website URL, redirect URIs, Developer Terms acceptance and access permissions; description, icons, support URL and deauthorization callback URL are optional.
evidence.quote: You must accept the Developer Terms of Service to build an integration with Clio.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage integration builders use the Clio Manage developer portal, separate from the Clio Platform portal used for Grow.
evidence.quote: If you're building a Clio Manage integration, you can use the Clio Manage developer portal.

evidence.claim: A free developer account is requested through a short form, after which a partnership team member follows up by email.
evidence.quote: a member of our developer partnership team will reach out with next steps via email.

evidence.claim: A seven-day trial account can be converted to a free developer account by application.
evidence.quote: you can apply to convert your trial account to a free developer account.

evidence.claim: No approval is needed before a public app developer begins building; the build stage is self-directed.
evidence.quote: You do not need to wait for approval before you begin building your integration.

evidence.claim: Building for your own practice or one firm requires login credentials on an existing paid Clio account, obtained from the firm's account admin.
evidence.quote: You will need to have access to login credentials on an existing, paid Clio account.

evidence.claim: The redirect_uri in an authorize request must match one of the URIs registered in the app's settings.
evidence.quote: The URL must match one of the redirect URLs specified in your application settings.

evidence.claim: Registered redirect URIs act as an explicit allow-list; a redirect to an unregistered URI fails.
evidence.quote: they act as an explicit allow-list, so any attempt to redirect to a URI not on the list will result in an error.

evidence.claim: PKCE is offered on the Clio Platform (Grow) form; Clio Manage PKCE support is unconfirmed.
evidence.quote: Enable Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) for enhanced security.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant; token exchange is a form-encoded POST to app.clio.com/oauth/token with key, secret, code and redirect_uri.
evidence.quote: Clio implements the OAuth 2.0 specification.

evidence.claim: Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last 30 days (expires_in 2592000); refresh tokens do not expire and should be stored encrypted.
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens do not expire; as a result, they should be encrypted and stored securely.

evidence.claim: A refresh request uses grant_type refresh_token plus client credentials; the documented response has a new access token and no new refresh token, so rotation is not shown.
evidence.quote: Below is a sample JSON response containing a refreshed access token:

evidence.claim: Developers select access permissions (scopes) at app creation, set each to read-only or read/write, and should request the smallest set needed.
evidence.quote: You should choose the smallest set necessary for your application to function properly

evidence.claim: Changing permissions later does not alter existing grants; users must re-authorize.
evidence.quote: you'll need to prompt your users to reauthorize your application

evidence.claim: Clio Identity's OpenID discovery document lists offline_access, offline, openid and clio_user_info; these are SSO scopes separate from Manage API permissions.
To start the security review, the developer emails api.partnerships@clio.com for a questionnaire; Clio aims to review within two business days.
evidence.quote: We aim to review within 2 business days.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage listing sequence: security questionnaire request, then demo to API Partnerships after approval, then listing form and draft review, then launch.
evidence.quote: After our Application Security and Compliance team has approved your app, send an email to our API Partnerships team (api.partnerships@clio.com) with a pre-recorded demo.

evidence.claim: App Integrations placement inside Clio Manage requires the app to be listed or approved for listing, plus working Add to Clio support; developers then email the App Integrations team with the app name and listing URL.
evidence.quote: your app must either be either listed on the Clio App Directory already, or you’ve been approved to be listed.

evidence.claim: App Directory launch requirements include passing security review, onboarding content, support for the latest two browser versions, and 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis.
evidence.quote: Demonstrate at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis for core functionality

evidence.claim: The launch process has four phases: security review, a 30-minute demo once security is signed off, a listing outline, and public launch.
evidence.quote: you'll be invited to book a 30-minute demo with our team.

evidence.claim: Clio may check that web apps support the latest two versions of major browsers, demonstrated before launch.
evidence.quote: We may ask for this to be demonstrated before launch.

evidence.claim: Clio offers no sandbox for the Manage API; developers test on their own developer account and should avoid customer accounts.
evidence.quote: Clio does not provide a test/sandbox environment at this time.

evidence.claim: An older help-center article says submission is by emailing api.partnerships@clio.com with a link and sample credentials, after which Clio emails documentation requirements.
evidence.quote: Once we've reviewed your integration, we'll email you with the required documentation.

evidence.claim: Default API rate limit is 50 requests per minute during peak hours, enforced per access token, with 429 responses beyond that; custom increases are not supported for applications.
evidence.quote: We do not support custom rate limit increases for applications at this time.

evidence.claim: No separate cap is stated for unreviewed or unlisted apps; higher limits apply off-peak.
evidence.quote: Rate limits are increased during off-peak hours

evidence.claim: Clio distinguishes public apps, which may be published to the App Directory, from private apps built for one client or firm and not listed.
evidence.quote: Private apps are meant to be apps built for the specific needs of a single client or law firm.

evidence.claim: Serving more than one region requires a separate Developer Application in each region; regional developer portals and OAuth hosts differ.
evidence.quote: The base URL must match the region of the Clio account you are connecting to.

evidence.claim: Integrations are local to each regional instance; a US integration does not serve Canadian customers and a token from one region is not valid in another.
evidence.quote: you can't, for example, create a US integration and have it work for Canadian Clio customers.

evidence.claim: When a token is revoked, Clio POSTs a JSON notice with client_id, user_id and access_token to the deauthorization callback URL.
evidence.quote: Clio will make a POST request to the specified URL.

evidence.claim: The developer portal at developers.clio.com/apps sits behind a Clio account OAuth login titled for the Clio Developer Portal (US).
Passing a security review is an entry requirement for apps in the App Directory listing process.
evidence.quote: Must pass a security review (as part of the app listing process)

evidence.claim: A community guide describes creating the app from Settings, then Developer Applications, on the US app host.
evidence.quote: Sign in to Clio and go to Settings → Developer Applications.

evidence.claim: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Clio (no 'clio' toolkit found), so the developer must supply their own Clio key and secret.

open_questions: No published timeline for App Directory review beyond the two-business-day questionnaire target; demo and listing timing are not given.
No user cap or install cap is documented for unlisted or private Clio Manage apps.
Not documented whether an unlisted public app can be installed by other firms without review.
Which Clio Manage permissions are sensitive or restricted, and whether write access triggers extra review, is not documented.
Whether PKCE is supported on the Clio Manage authorize flow is unconfirmed; the PKCE option found is on the Clio Platform (Grow) form.
Whether refresh tokens rotate on refresh is not stated.
Developer account approval criteria and timing are not published; the form contents were not reviewed.
The authorize endpoint probe used a placeholder client_id; Clio's exact invalid-client response was not observed.
